name: Primary Hypereosinophilic Syndrome

criteria.description: Persistent eosinophilia >1.5 × 10^9/L for more than 6 months
Evidence of organ involvement or dysfunction attributable to eosinophilia
Exclusion of secondary causes of eosinophilia such as parasitic infections, allergies, and other hematologic malignancies
Bone marrow biopsy showing eosinophilic hyperplasia without evidence of clonal myeloid neoplasm
Absence of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, or FGFR1 fusion genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent eosinophilia >1.5 × 10^9/L for >6 months with organ damage attributable to eosinophilia and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of secondary and clonal eosinophilic disorders.

searchTerms: increased white blood cells type eosinophils

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic cardiac involvement leading to restrictive cardiomyopathy
searchTerms: heart muscle fibrosis due to eosinophils
thickened heart tissue from eosinophil buildup
pruritic rash caused by eosinophilic inflammation

common.symptomName: Eosinophilic pneumonitis causing cough and dyspnea
searchTerms: cough and shortness of breath from lung eosinophilia
eosinophilic lung disease causing breathing issues

common.symptomName: Gastrointestinal eosinophilic infiltration causing abdominal pain
Peripheral neuropathy due to eosinophilic infiltration
searchTerms: peripheral nerve problems due to eosinophilic infiltration
numbness or weakness from eosinophil-related neuropathy

occasional.symptomName: Eosinophilic hepatitis with elevated liver enzymes
occasional.notes: Hepatic involvement is less common but reported
searchTerms: raised liver enzymes from eosinophilic hepatitis

occasional.symptomName: Thromboembolic events secondary to eosinophil-mediated endothelial damage
searchTerms: clotting events linked to eosinophilic endothelial damage

occasional.symptomName: Eosinophilic gastritis with nausea and vomiting
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from eosinophilic gastritis

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system eosinophilic infiltration causing seizures
searchTerms: seizures due to eosinophilic brain involvement

laboratory: Elevated serum vitamin B12 and tryptase levels
Bone marrow eosinophilic hyperplasia without clonal markers
imaging: MRI for cardiac and CNS involvement
other: Tissue biopsy showing eosinophilic infiltration and fibrosis
Exclusion of secondary causes such as parasitic infections and allergic diseases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of clonal genetic abnormalities (e.g., PDGFRA fusion gene)
Myeloproliferative features on bone marrow biopsy
Identification of underlying cause such as parasitic infection, allergic disease, or drug reaction
Resolution of eosinophilia after treatment of underlying cause

redFlags: Rapidly progressive heart failure due to eosinophilic endomyocardial fibrosis
Thromboembolic complications secondary to eosinophil-mediated endothelial injury
